assessmentSummary.identity: Hollow-to-Arch Roll is one complete controlled floor cycle: begin in a declared supine hollow shape, roll as one long body without hand or foot push-off to a declared prone arch shape, then return through the same controlled whole-body roll to the declared supine hollow start. A cycle is not a static hold, a rock, a log roll, a tuck roll, a forward/backward roll, a shoulder roll, an arch rock, a bridge, or a multi-cycle conditioning drill.
currentCardFindings: Source 71 names a hollow-to-arch roll but does not define the start/finish shapes, side rule, contact boundary, count unit, surface, exit, dose, fatigue, relationships, evidence, or candidate review state.

The existing hollow-family audit correctly distinguishes this orientation-changing roll from static hollow holds. The card must retain that distinction rather than silently treating a roll, rock, partial turn, or static shape as interchangeable.

Three direct URLs inherited from Source 71 are traceable candidates only; no playback, availability, embedding, exact match, captions, accessibility, safety, quality, reviewer, or approval conclusion is inferred.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Start in a declared supine hollow shape on a clean stable mat or floor. Roll as one long body without hand or foot push-off to a declared prone arch shape, then return through the same controlled whole-body roll to the declared hollow start. One full hollow-to-arch-to-hollow return is one cycle. Pause and reset between cycles as needed. Record direction, cycles, surface, pace, shape quality, orientation response, symptoms, and rest. Static holds, rocks, log/tuck/shoulder/forward/backward rolls, bridges, loaded rolling, assessments, and other changed tasks require their own reviewed variant or definition.
